{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-nqes","title":"MessagesStore POST stores caller map; from is spoofable","description":"File: rust/lichen-client/src/msg.rs (MessagesStore::post_inbox)

POST /msg/inbox keeps the decoded caller CBOR map (after canned expansion and id assign) as both the sent record and the inbox record. It does not build a server-authoritative receive document.

Spec 18.1.2 inbox items are {id, from, ts, body}. from is the sender identity. The Python oracle (python/src/lichen/coap/resources/messaging.py render_post) has a SECURITY comment and body.pop("from", None) so the client cannot spoof sender.

Rust never strips from, never stamps receiver time, and never allowlists keys. A mesh POST can:

1. Set from to an arbitrary IPv6 string (sender spoofing).
2. Set read to true so unread_count() (spec 18.1.2) skips the message.
3. Leak send-only keys (to, canned, ack, priority, text) into GET /msg/inbox.

Fix: strip or ignore untrusted keys; set from from the transport/peer, not the payload; persist only the spec receive fields (plus server id/ts). Match the Python from strip at minimum.

Perspectives: security, correctness.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"me@mark.atwood.name","created_at":"2026-08-26T17:25:29.149762Z","created_by":"grok","updated_at":"2026-08-26T17:25:29.149762Z","labels":["codereview"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-nqes","depends_on_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-l1qw.10.14.2","type":"discovered-from","created_at":"2026-08-26T17:25:29.516469Z","created_by":"grok","metadata":"{}"}]}

new_value: POST /msg/inbox strips payload from, rebinds from transport peer, and persists spec 18.1.2 receive fields only. Tests cover spoof, rebind, duplicate keys, read unread, send-key leak.
